A relatively literal English rendering of the Latin text of the Instituta Cnuti, created for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model made by Anthropic. It is a crib to help the reader with the Latin, and should not be treated as a separate translation. Liebermann’s kinds of type (bold, spaced, smaller type, round brackets) are carried over onto the English words that render the marked Latin

div.head: In Cn III 3
div.ab: Qui calumniatur de hloth, sí negauerit, ita sé purget: acceptis undecim hominibus, et ipse sit duodecimus; aut despectum calumniantis persoluat et duas libras pro forisfactura ei det qui habet consuetudines suas.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 613 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

div.ab: Whoever is accused of hloth [band], if he denies it, shall clear himself thus: having taken eleven men, he himself being the twelfth; or he shall pay the accuser's contempt [fine] and give two pounds as forfeiture to him who has his customs.
